title: Most people read Joseph’s dreams like a highlight reel.
paragraphs: Most people read Joseph’s dreams like a highlight reel.
But they completely miss the part that cost him everything.
Joseph didn’t just have dreams—he had revelation.
“Behold, we were binding sheaves in the field, and lo, my sheaf arose and stood upright…” (Genesis 37:7)
“Behold, the sun and the moon and eleven stars were bowing down to me.” (Genesis 37:9)
But here’s what most people don’t realize…

God will show you where you’re going
before He shows you what it will take to get there.
Because if Joseph had seen the pit…
he might have run from the calling.
They threw him into a pit.
And then they sold him like property.
Genesis 37:28 — “They drew Joseph up and lifted him out of the pit, and sold him…”
And here’s the part you try to ignore:
This is where shallow faith collapses.
“If God is with you, life will be easy.”

Joseph was closest to God
when his life looked the most abandoned.
“You meant evil against me, but God meant it for good…” (Genesis 50:20)
That’s a revelation forged in suffering.
You’re frustrated because God showed you something real…
but you’re offended by the path He chose to get you there.
You think the delay means denial.
You think the pain means punishment.
Joseph’s story is not about success.
God wasn’t trying to promote Joseph.
He was trying to prepare him.

Because a throne without character
becomes destruction.
You have sinned against a holy God.
“For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.” (Romans 3:23)
Jesus wasn’t just thrown into a pit.
“God shows His love for us in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.” (Romans 5:8)
Jesus took the punishment you deserved.
“In Him we have redemption through His blood, the forgiveness of sins…” (Ephesians 1:7)

Will you keep chasing dreams
while ignoring your sin?

Or will you surrender to the One
who gave His life to redeem you?
Because the real tragedy isn’t a delayed dream.
